clue.text: Cockney was hovering, about to strike punch, cutting loose

indicators.note: about tells us the Cockney word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: was hovering is HUNG, and a Cockney drops the H to say 'ung
to strike is to hit
to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

explanation.surface: A Cockney who had been hesitating about throwing a punch finally lets fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney convention drops an initial H, so HUNG becomes UNG; 'about' puts HIT and CHIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhitching is untying or unfastening, which is the same as cutting something loose.

clue.text: Wooden bar one puts up then another jumps?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, each of the two small wooden crosspieces resting on the stumps

definitions.text: one puts up then another jumps?
definitions.meaning: a surety puts up money to free an accused person, who may then abscond, jumping it

explanation.walkthrough: A bail is one of the small wooden pieces on top of the cricket stumps; in court, bail is the money put up to release someone, and to 'jump bail' is to flee before trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bail is a wooden crosspiece, and legal bail is posted by a surety and skipped by an absconder.

clue.text: Line of cars picked up TV signal

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: auto is a car and a line of them waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: A traffic jam is caught on television.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is the prompting screen that feeds a television presenter their lines, a signal of what to say.

clue.text: Time machine era stopping sooner or later

indicators.note: both words are made to stop one letter earlier than they should, losing their last letters

parts.note: the TARDIS is the time machine in the TV series Doctor Who
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's time machine halts its journey through an era, sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping sooner' cuts the final letter from each piece: TARDIS loses its S and ERA its A, giving TARDI and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardier means more delayed or slower in arriving, so it comes later.

clue.text: Cites novel that's understood by one in vain

indicators.note: in tells us the two short pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of cites take a new order

parts.note: if you got something you understood it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a work of fiction is only grasped by a single conceited person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the clue's first word as ESTIC; 'in' splits that after its E. 'vain' alone is the definition, not 'in vain'.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotistic person is conceited and self-absorbed, just as a vain person is.

clue.text: Secure nick

definitions.meaning: to achieve or gain something, as in scoring a win

explanation.definitionFit: To notch up is to secure a result, and a notch is a small V-shaped nick cut in something.

clue.text: Cheers on champion returning for award

indicators.note: on places the word for cheers after the other piece
returning means the word for champion is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: champion and fab are both informal British words for excellent
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Applause for a winner who comes back to collect a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'champion!' and 'fab!' both mean marvellous; 'returning' makes BAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A BAFTA is a British film and television award, so it is one example of an award.

clue.text: Junk adoptable as pleasure craft

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it and break it up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A Chinese junk could be taken on as a leisure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like the Chinese sailing ship, fitting 'pleasure craft', but here it means scrap and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalboat is a small boat moved by pedalling, used for leisure on lakes, so a pleasure craft.

clue.text: Head of group, in base, struggles the most with it?

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word
in shows the word for struggles goes inside the word for base

parts.note: a root is the base or foundation of something
vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: A gang leader, back at headquarters, fights hardest to stay fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' is dated slang for fashionable; 'in' signals one piece sitting inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooviest is slang for most fashionable or trendy, the most up to date or with it.

clue.text: City bank may forgo profit also, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A financial institution might give up its earnings as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is a major city in Japan, its former imperial capital.

clue.text: Bay with Gibraltar to the west's showing up

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards
showing up means appearing within the words, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A bay with the Rock of Gibraltar on its western side comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up' finds THGIB across 'with Gibraltar'; 'to the west' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a long curved stretch of coast forming a wide bay, like the Great Australian Bight.

clue.text: Odd articles from old trains and one taxi drivers' association

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway in Britain
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cab is a taxi
RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Stray items turn up from old railway trains and a taxi drivers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is a jumble of miscellaneous small ornaments and objects, an assortment of odd articles.

clue.text: Religious devotions recalled well in mind of German

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to be sane is to be mentally well
von is German for of

explanation.surface: Prayers remembered fondly by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal turns both pieces: SANEVON read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine successive days.

clue.text: Stands by nothing that's written in New Yorkers' volumes?

indicators.note: written in means placed inside, so the letter for nothing goes inside the volumes

parts.note: liters is the American spelling of litres, a measure of volume
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone stands waiting while nothing gets written in New York's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volumes' looks like books, but means measures of capacity, spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly, standing by without purpose.

clue.text: Sharp movement of rabbit straddling pole

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so the word for rabbit goes round the pole

parts.note: in British slang to rabbit is to chatter, as is to yak
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A rabbit jumps quickly over a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for talk on and on, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yank is a sudden hard pull, a sharp jerking movement.

clue.text: Jabber, meeting British spies, making conjecture

parts.note: a hypo is a hypodermic needle, something that jabs
THE SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's foreign spy agency

explanation.surface: Gossip about an encounter with British agents is just speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like a chatterer but is a needle that jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation or supposition, a conjecture.

clue.text: States time for practice

parts.note: the US, the United States
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Countries set a time for doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: Let's honour newspaper's capital coverage? Nothing more

parts.note: a hat covers the head, the capital or top
of FT, FT being the Financial Times newspaper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A newspaper praises headgear in the capital city, and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means head, so hats are head coverage; 'newspaper's' is read as 'of FT'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats off to is an exclamation saluting someone, inviting us to honour them.

clue.text: CCTV got Italian's corrupt electoral practice

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or distorted, so the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Security cameras caught an Italian engaging in electoral fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical voting is backing a candidate one does not prefer in order to defeat another, an electoral strategy.

clue.text: The ale abandoned quietly?

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Beer left behind without a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the dregs of ale left behind in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the dated term for liquor left at the bottom of a glass after drinking.

clue.text: Clocked high speed after ascent finished off

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent reads upwards, so the word for high speed is reversed

parts.note: a ton is a hundred miles per hour
iced is slang for killed, finished off

explanation.surface: A speeding car is caught on camera after climbing a hill and then crashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clocked' suggests a speed camera, but means spotted; a ton is British slang for 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock someone is informal for seeing or spotting them, i.e. to have noticed.

clue.text: Settled for keeping silent at first as most celebrated?

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the word for settled holds the letter

parts.note: alit means landed, settled

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word silent

explanation.surface: Agreed to stay quiet at first, as the most famous people do.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, the most celebrated people.

clue.text: Rather slow tailless bird initially hovering within reach

indicators.note: tailless means the bird loses its final letter

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

indicators.note: within means one letter goes inside the phrase for reach

parts.note: to get to a place is to reach it

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word hovering

explanation.surface: A slow-moving bird with no tail hovers within range.
explanation.walkthrough: Larghetto is an Italian tempo marking; 'tailless' trims the bird and 'within' puts the H inside the phrase for reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is a musical tempo marking meaning fairly slow, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: Kind, frail, English Sikh bent down a lot

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentle, frail Englishman and a Sikh are stooped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like low or depressed, but means swallow drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink like a fish is the idiom for drinking heavily, downing a lot.

clue.text: Insects like cake? He loves carrots

parts.note: bugs are insects
bunny read as bun-ny, like a bun or cake

explanation.surface: Bugs resembling cake are adored by a carrot fan.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNNY is read whimsically as an adjective, 'bun-like', from bun, a small cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs Bunny is the cartoon rabbit famous for munching carrots.

clue.text: Miserable old boy's going round not giving out perfume

parts.note: dour means gloomy, miserable
Les is a boy's name, so the boy's is Les's, roaming about

explanation.surface: A gloomy old lad wanders about without wearing any scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Les is a man's name, so 'boy's' gives LES'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means having no smell, so it gives off no scent or perfume.

clue.text: With facility that's extra small inside incorporating doctor's official residence

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the doctor goes inside too
inside puts the extra letter within the word for facility

parts.note: easy means done with facility, without effort
an extra S, for small
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: An easy facility with an extra-small extension, including a doctor's official home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra' tells us the S is added as an extra letter on top of those already there; 'inside' and 'incorporating' both mean insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the official residence and offices of an ambassador abroad.

clue.text: Cotton on large rings forming shelter

parts.note: to twig and to cotton on both mean to realise
two O shapes are rings

explanation.surface: Cotton is wound in big loops to make a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' is British slang for catch on or understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A twigloo is a makeshift shelter built of twigs, especially by road protesters living in trees.

clue.text: Archdeacon following American in service for Lent?

indicators.note: following places the archdeacon's title after the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier in the armed services
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman comes after an American at a Lenten service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the church season, but means handed over; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lent has been handed over to another for a time, so it has been given.

clue.text: Charges informally for crossing thoroughfare

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the informal word goes around the street

parts.note: cos is an informal shortening of because, meaning for
ST is street, a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Fees are charged, casually, for walking across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs are the prices or fees demanded, the charges for something.
